# Total.js conventions: every page

> How Total.js 5 applications are written: ES5 over ES6, Total.js prototypes and Tangular first, no imports from Node.js, actions named Collection|verb, routes in controllers, DATA queries, PostgreSQL scripts and jComponent components loaded with COMPONENTATOR(). Learned from production Total.js 5 apps and the official style guide.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/conventions/main/README.md

# Total.js conventions

How Total.js 5 applications are written, learned from real production apps and from the official style guide. It is a reference for people and for AI agents: read the zone you are working in, copy the pattern, keep the names.

Every rule comes with an example taken from the code of the Total.js apps (CMS, Dashboard, OpenPlatform, Todomator) or from the [official guidelines](https://github.com/totaljs-es/guidelines). Where the two differ, the page says so.

## Zones

Each zone is a folder. Read only the one you need.

| Zone | What it covers |
|---|---|
| [`general/`](general) | Project layout, JavaScript style, naming. Applies everywhere. |
| [`backend/`](backend) | Actions, routes, authentication, definitions, modules, gotchas of the server. |
| [`database/`](database) | PostgreSQL scripts and how the code queries them with `DATA`. |
| [`frontend/`](frontend) | jComponent components (use the existing ones, `COMPONENTATOR()`), plugins with UI, views and layouts, CSS. |

## Pages

- general: [project-structure](general/project-structure.md), [javascript-style](general/javascript-style.md)
- backend: [actions](backend/actions.md), [routes-and-auth](backend/routes-and-auth.md), [definitions-and-modules](backend/definitions-and-modules.md), [gotchas](backend/gotchas.md)
- database: [sql-scripts](database/sql-scripts.md), [queries](database/queries.md)
- frontend: [components](frontend/components.md), [plugins-ui](frontend/plugins-ui.md), [views-and-layout](frontend/views-and-layout.md), [css](frontend/css.md)

## For AI agents

- [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md): how to use these pages and the rules for every change (also `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md` and `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, which point to it).
- [`llms.txt`](llms.txt): an index with a link to every page; [`llms-full.txt`](llms-full.txt): every page in one file.
- Skills to write and to review code with these conventions: `.claude/skills/` and `.agents/skills/`.

## Principles

1. **ES5 over ES6**: `var`, `function`, classic loops. ES6 only when there is no ES5 way.
2. **Total.js first**: prototypes (`'{0}'.format()`, `findItem()`, `parseJSON()`...) in the backend and Tangular in the frontend, before any other function.
3. **No imports from Node.js**: use `Total.Fs`, `Total.Path`, `Total.Crypto`... instead of `require()`.
4. Follow the code that is already next to yours. A new file looks like its neighbours.
5. Keep names short, lowercase and the same across projects: `id`, `name`, `body`, `dtcreated`, `items`.
6. Declare input once (`input:` / `params:`) and let the framework validate it. The action body trusts what it receives.
7. Keep routes in one place (`controllers/` or the plugin's `index.js`), logic in actions, data access in `DATA`.
8. Add no dependency that the framework already covers.
9. Check what you changed: `node --check file.js`, then run the app and call the route.

## Versions

Written for **Total.js 5** (`total5` on npm). The official guidelines were written for Total.js 4 (`NEWSCHEMA`, `var`); the pages mark the places where Total.js 5 code differs. Do not assume a Total.js 4 API exists in version 5: check the framework source or an existing app.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/conventions/main/AGENTS.md

# AGENTS.md

This repository is a reference of conventions for Total.js 5 applications. Read it before writing or changing Total.js code.

## How to use it

1. Open [README.md](README.md) and pick the zone you work in: `general/`, `backend/`, `database/` or `frontend/`.
2. Read only the pages of that zone. Each page has rules with examples taken from real apps.
3. Copy the pattern of the nearest existing file in the project you are editing; use these pages to decide what is idiomatic.

## Rules that apply to every change

- Total.js 5 only. Do not use Total.js 4 APIs.
- ES5 over ES6: `var`, `function`, classic loops, `'{0}'.format()` instead of template literals. ES6 only when there is no ES5 way.
- Use Total.js prototypes (`findItem`, `format`, `parseJSON`, `slug`, `isEmail`...) in the backend and Tangular templates in the frontend before any other function.
- Do not `require()` Node.js modules: use `Total.Fs`, `Total.Path`, `Total.Crypto`, `Total.OS`, `Total.Zlib`, etc.
- Tabs, semicolons, `'` for short strings, lowercase file names with `-`.
- Actions are `NEWACTION('Collection|verb', { name, input, params, permissions, action })`.
- Routes live in `controllers/` or in the plugin's `index.js`: `ROUTE('+API ? -name --> Collection|verb')`.
- Data goes through `DATA` with `.promise($)`; ids are `UID()`, dates are `NOW`.
- Frontend: use an existing jComponent component (catalogue: https://forge.totaljs.es/es/components/, markdown at `https://forge.totaljs.es/en/components/<name>.md`); if none exists, create a reusable `COMPONENT('name', ...)`. Load components only with `COMPONENTATOR()`.
- Every text for people is `@(Text)`.
- After editing JavaScript run `node --check file.js`; start the app and call the route you changed.

## Layout

- `general/`, `backend/`, `database/`, `frontend/`: the pages, one folder per zone.
- `llms.txt` (index) and `llms-full.txt` (every page in one file): for models. They are generated, do not edit them by hand.
- `scripts/llms.js`: builds the two files above and lists the pages in order.
- `.claude/skills/` and `.agents/skills/`: the skills to write and to review Total.js 5 code with these conventions.
- `tests/`: tests of the files for agents and of the links of the pages.

## Using these conventions from another project

Point your agent at `llms.txt` (an index with a link to every page) or at `llms-full.txt` (all the pages at once):

- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/conventions/main/llms.txt
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/conventions/main/llms-full.txt

A project can add a line to its own `AGENTS.md`: "Follow the Total.js 5 conventions of https://github.com/totaljs-es/conventions".

## Checking this repository

- `npm test` checks that the pointers and skills exist, that every page is listed in `llms.txt`, that `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` match the pages, and that every link works.
- After you change or add a page, run `npm run llms` and `npm test`. A new page is also added to the list in `scripts/llms.js`.

## Keeping these pages true

Every rule here comes from code that exists. When you add a rule, add an example from a real file or from the framework source, and say which.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/conventions/main/general/project-structure.md

# Project structure

A Total.js 5 app is a folder that the framework loads by convention. Put each kind of file where the framework (and the next reader) expects it.

```
index.js            starts the app: require('total5'); F.run(options)
config              settings, one "key : value" per line
package.json        "total5" is the runtime dependency
controllers/        routes: exports.install = function() { ROUTE(...) }
definitions/        auth.js, init.js, func.js, db.js: loaded at start, no exports
modules/            integrations with other systems (cdn, openplatform, tapi...)
plugins/<name>/     a feature: index.js (server), index.html (UI), schemas/, public/
schemas/            actions that are not part of a plugin
views/              layout and pages (HTML with @{...} directives)
public/             static files: default.css, default.js, img/, fonts/
database.sql        the full schema; changes go to dated files next to it
```

Optional, when the app is shipped: `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yaml`, `bundle.sh` (writes `--bundles--/app.bundle`), `license.txt`, `readme.md`.

## index.js

The start script is the same in every app and has almost no logic:

```js
require('total5');

var options = {};
options.release = process.argv.indexOf('--release') !== -1;
options.servicemode = process.argv.indexOf('--service') !== -1 || process.argv.indexOf('--servicemode') !== -1;

F.run(options);
```

Run it with `node index.js 8000` (add `--release` for release mode).

## Where things go

- **A route** goes in `controllers/*.js` or in `plugins/<name>/index.js`, never inside an action file.
- **Business logic** is a `NEWACTION` in `schemas/` (or `plugins/<name>/schemas/`).
- **Shared helpers** hang from `FUNC` (`FUNC.notify`, `FUNC.save`) and live in `definitions/func.js`.
- **Shared state in memory** hangs from `MAIN` (the app) or `REPO` (cached lookups, e.g. `REPO.tags`).
- **Startup work** (config defaults, loading caches, registering UI components) goes in `ON('ready', ...)` in `definitions/init.js`.
- **Authentication** is one `AUTH(...)` in `definitions/auth.js`.

## Files and folders

- All lowercase, words separated by `-`, never `_`: `search-results.html`.
- Static files by type: `/img/`, `/js/`, `/css/`, `/fonts/`, `/videos/`.
- One plugin per feature, named after the feature: `plugins/redirects`, `plugins/users`.
- Generated output (`--bundles--/`, `tmp/`, `databases/`) is not edited by hand.

## Checks

- `node --check path/to/file.js` for every JavaScript file you change.
- Start the app and call the route you touched. If the project has no test script, do not say tests passed.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/conventions/main/general/javascript-style.md

# JavaScript style

Source: the [official guidelines](https://github.com/totaljs-es/guidelines) plus what the Total.js 5 apps do. Three rules come first, because they decide most of the code you write:

1. **ES5 over ES6.** Always prefer the ES5 way.
2. **Total.js first.** Use the framework's prototypes (backend) and Tangular (frontend) before any other function.
3. **No imports from Node.js.** Use the modules Total.js already exposes.

## 1. ES5 over ES6

Write `var`, `function`, classic loops and string helpers. Use an ES6 feature only when there is no ES5 way to do the same.

| Prefer | Instead of |
|---|---|
| `var item = ...;` | `let` / `const` in a function |
| `function(item) { ... }` | `item => ...` |
| `for (var i = 0; i < arr.length; i++)` | `for...of`, `forEach`, `map`, `filter`, `reduce` chains |
| `'Hello {0}'.format(name)` | template literal `` `Hello ${name}` `` |
| `var a = obj.a;` | destructuring, spread, optional chaining |
| `arr.findItem('id', id)` | `arr.find(x => x.id === id)` |

```js
// good
var item = db.redirects.findItem('id', model.id);
if (!item) {
	$.invalid(404);
	return;
}

// avoid
const item = db.redirects.find(m => m.id === model.id);
```

Notes:

- `async` / `await` stays where the framework's own code uses it (`await DATA.find(...).promise($)`): there the ES5 alternative is a callback chain (`.callback($)`), which is also valid when it reads better.
- Some source apps use `let`, arrows and template literals. Do not copy those from them: write the ES5 form.
- `const` is for module-level constants only: `const ADMIN = { id: 'admin', sa: true };`.
- **Never `for...in` over an array**: Total.js adds enumerable methods to `Array.prototype`. Use a classic `for` loop.

## 2. Total.js first

### Backend: prototypes

Total.js extends `String`, `Array`, `Number` and `Date`. Before writing a helper, a loop or a regular expression, check whether a prototype does it. These exist in Total.js 5:

- **String:** `format`, `parseJSON`, `parseInt`, `parseFloat`, `parseBoolean`, `parseDate`, `parseConfig`, `parseCSV`, `parseXML`, `slug`, `capitalize`, `pluralize`, `max`, `toSearch`, `toKeywords`, `removeTags`, `encode`, `decode`, `safehtml`, `md5`, `sha1`, `sha256`, `hash`, `crc32`, `encrypt`, `decrypt`, `isEmail`, `isPhone`, `isURL`, `isJSON`, `isUID`, `isGUID`, `isNumber`, `isBase64`, `isXSS`, `isSQLInjection`, `indent`, `tslash`.
- **Array:** `findItem`, `findIndex`, `findAll`, `findValue`, `remove`, `quicksort`, `trim`, `first`, `last`, `take`, `skip`, `limit`, `group`, `random`, `wait`, `async`.
- **Number:** `format`, `currency`, `round`, `floor`, `fixed`, `between`, `padLeft`, `padRight`, `filesize`, `pluralize`, `discount`, `parseDate`.
- **Date:** `format`, `add`, `diff`, `extend`, `toUTC`, `setTimeZone`, `parseDate`.

```js
var name = '{0} {1}'.format(first, last);                  // not a template literal
var index = items.findIndex('id', id);                     // not findIndex(m => m.id === id)
var data = text.parseJSON();                               // not try { JSON.parse(text) } catch
var slug = title.slug();                                   // not a hand-made regex
var keywords = body.toKeywords();
if (email.isEmail()) { ... }
```

If you are about to write a utility, search the framework source (`utils.js`) first. The helpers of `U.` (e.g. `U.normalize()`) and the globals (`UID()`, `NOW`, `CONF`, `DATA`) come before your own.

### Frontend: Tangular

In jComponent code and plugin HTML, build text and markup with **Tangular** templates (`{{ value }}`, `{{ foreach m in value }}`, `{{ if }}`) and its helpers, not with string concatenation or DOM-building code.

```html
<script type="text/html">
	{{ foreach m in value }}
	<figure class="exec" data-exec="?/edit" data-id="{{ m.id }}">{{ m.url }}</figure>
	{{ end }}
</script>
```

See [plugins-ui](../frontend/plugins-ui.md).

## 3. No imports from Node.js

Do not `require()` Node.js modules. Total.js exposes them:

| Instead of | Use |
|---|---|
| `require('fs')` | `Total.Fs` |
| `require('path')` | `Total.Path` |
| `require('crypto')` | `Total.Crypto` |
| `require('os')` | `Total.OS` |
| `require('http')` / `require('https')` | `Total.Http` / `Total.Https` (for requests prefer `RESTBuilder`) |
| `require('child_process')` | `Total.Child` |
| `require('zlib')` | `Total.Zlib` |
| `require('url')`, `require('util')`, `require('stream')` | `Total.Url`, `Total.Util`, `Total.Stream` |

Also available: `Total.Cluster`, `Total.Dns`, `Total.Net`, `Total.Tls`, `Total.Worker` and `Total.isBundle` (since v0.0.50). Third-party packages are the last resort: the framework usually covers the need.

```js
// good
var file = Total.Path.join(F.tmpdir, 'data.json');

// avoid
const Path = require('path');
```

(The official guide shows `const Path = require('path')`. That was for Total.js 4; in Total.js 5 use `Total.Path`.)

## Formatting

- Indent with **tabs** (width 4). No trailing white space.
- End every statement with `;`.
- Short strings in `'` apostrophes.
- A condition with one statement has no braces and no blank line:

```js
if (!item)
	return;

item && refresh();     // fine for a simple expression
```

## Variables and names

- Common names, the same in every project: `id`, `name`, `value`, `email`, `items` / `arr` (a collection), `item`, `tmp`, `dtcreated`, `dtupdated`.

| Thing | Convention | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Files, folders | lowercase, `-` | `form-offer.html` |
| Actions | `Collection\|verb` (pipe; exposed to MCP as `Collection_verb`) | `Redirects\|save` |
| Schemas | plural, first letter upper case; `@Name` for a reusable input | `NEWSCHEMA('Tickets', ...)`, `'@Group'` |
| API routes | lowercase, `_` between collection and verb | `tickets_create` |
| Plugins, components, `FUNC.`, `MAIN.`, `REPO.` keys | lowercase | `FUNC.refreshtags` |
| Table and column names | lowercase | `tbl_user`, `dtcreated` |

## Framework globals

Use the globals that exist instead of writing your own: `UID()` for identifiers, `NOW` for the current date, `CONF` for config, `DATA` for the database, `EMPTYARRAY` / `EMPTYOBJECT` for read-only defaults.

```js
model.id = UID();
model.dtcreated = NOW;
```

## Comments

A comment says why, in one or two lines, above the code it explains. Do not narrate what the next line does.

## Dependencies

Avoid adding any. If the framework has a helper (`RESTBuilder`, `FILESTORAGE`, `U.*`, `DATA`, a prototype), use it.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/conventions/main/backend/actions.md

# Actions

An action is one unit of server logic: a name, the input it accepts, who may call it, and a function. Define it with `NEWACTION` in a `schemas/` file.

```js
NEWACTION('Redirects|save', {
	name: 'Save redirect',
	input: 'id,*url,*target,permanent:Boolean',
	permissions: 'redirects,admin',
	action: function($, model) {

		if (model.id) {
			var item = MAIN.db.redirects.findItem('id', model.id);
			if (!item) {
				$.invalid(404);
				return;
			}
			item.dtupdated = NOW;
			item.url = model.url;
		} else {
			model.id = UID();
			model.dtcreated = NOW;
			MAIN.db.redirects.push(model);
		}

		FUNC.save();
		$.success();
	}
});
```

## Naming

`Collection|verb`, collection in plural and capitalized: `Tickets|list`, `Groups|create`, `Users|remove`. Separate the two parts with a pipe `|`.

The pipe is the convention because of MCP: the MCP router of Total.js 5 documents actions as `Notes|create` and exposes them as the tool `Notes_create` (tool names allow only letters, digits, `_` and `-`). The apps used as source for these pages (CMS, OpenPlatform, Todomator) write `Tickets/list` with a slash; their examples are shown here with a pipe. Use the pipe in new code, so the name an MCP client sees matches the action.

The usual verbs:

| Verb | Does | Input |
|---|---|---|
| `list` | returns a collection, often with `autoquery` | query string |
| `read` | returns one record | `params: '*id:UID'` |
| `create` | inserts, answers with the new id | `input` |
| `update` | modifies one record | `params` + `input` |
| `save` | create or update by `id` | `input` with optional `id` |
| `remove` | deletes or flags one record | `params` |

Always give the action a human `name:` ("Save redirect"): it is used in logs and tools.

## Input and params

- `input:` is the body, `params:` is the route parameters (`{id}`), `query:` is the query string.
- A text spec: `'*name,color:Color,icon:Icon,permissions:[String]'`. A leading `*` makes a field required. After `:` goes the type (`Boolean`, `Number`, `UID`, `Email`, `Phone`, `Color`, `Date`, `String(100)`, `[String]`).
- Reuse a definition with a named schema and `@`:

```js
NEWSCHEMA('@Group', '*name,color:Color,icon:Icon,reference,permissions:[String]');

NEWACTION('Groups|create', {
	name: 'Create group',
	input: '@Group',
	action: async function($, model) { /* ... */ }
});
```

- Route parameters arrive in `$.params`, not as an argument: `$.params.id`.
- A list typed `*field:[String]` is required: an empty list counts as missing. If empty is valid, drop the `*`.

## Answering

| Call | Use |
|---|---|
| `$.callback(data)` | return data (a record, a list, an id) |
| `$.success()` / `$.success(id)` | the success answer of the app (`DEF.onSuccess`: by default `{ success: true }`, with the value if you pass one) |
| `$.invalid(404)` | not found; the number is the HTTP status |
| `$.invalid('@(Text for the user)')` | validation or business error; `@(...)` marks it for translation |

Call exactly one of them, then `return`. An action that never answers hangs the request.

## Permissions

`permissions: 'redirects,admin'` allows users that have any of those permissions. Put it on every action that is not public, even when the route is already authorized.

## Async and data

Actions are `async` when they await `DATA` calls. Pass `$` to `.promise($)` so errors answer the request for you:

```js
action: async function($) {
	var params = $.params;
	var model = await DATA.read('op.tbl_group').id(params.id).error('@(Group not found)').promise($);
	$.callback(model);
}
```

See [queries](../database/queries.md) for `DATA`.

## Calling one action from another

`$.action('Items|types').promise()` (or `ACTION('Items|types', model).promise()` outside a request). Keep shared pieces in an action instead of copying code.

## Keep an action small

If one action grows beyond what fits on a screen, move the parts to `FUNC.` helpers or to other actions. Large filter builders (e.g. a `makefilter($, builder)` function inside the schema) stay next to the actions that use them.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/conventions/main/backend/routes-and-auth.md

# Routes and authentication

## Where routes live

In `exports.install` of a file in `controllers/` or of a plugin's `index.js`. One line per route, aligned in columns.

```js
exports.install = function() {

	// Tickets
	ROUTE('+API    ?       -tickets                   --> Tickets|list');
	ROUTE('+API    ?       -tickets_detail/{id}       --> Tickets|read');
	ROUTE('+API    ?       +tickets_create            --> Tickets|create', 1024 * 10);
	ROUTE('+API    ?       +tickets_update/{id}       --> Tickets|update', 1024 * 10);
	ROUTE('+API    ?       -tickets_remove/{id}       --> Tickets|remove');

};
```

Group the lines with a short comment per collection.

## Reading an API route

```
ROUTE('+API    ?    +tickets_create    --> Tickets|create', 1024 * 10);
        |      |     |                     |                |
        |      |     |                     |                max body size in bytes
        |      |     |                     the action
        |      |     "+" the request has a body (input), "-" it has none
        |      the URL of the endpoint; "?" is replaced by CONF.$api ("/api/" by default)
        "+" only for logged-in users; without it the route is public
```

- Endpoint names are lowercase with `_`: `tickets_create`, `users_remove/{id}`. `{id}` fills `$.params.id`.
- Use `-` for reads and removals, `+` for creates and updates.
- A plugin may bind the endpoint to its own base: `ROUTE('+API /setup/ -users --> Users|list')`.
- Without a size, the default body limit applies. Give a limit to routes that take larger bodies.

## Other routes

```js
ROUTE('+GET    /setup/', setup);         // a page, only for logged-in users
ROUTE('POST    /notify/', notify);       // a public route with a handler function
ROUTE('+POST    ?/upload/    @upload <10MB    --> Files|insert');   // an upload: @upload for multipart, <10MB for the size
```

A handler function is `function($)`. Prefer an API route plus an action; use a plain handler for pages, files and webhooks.

## A route declared in the action

`NEWACTION` also accepts `route: 'API ?'` (or `route: true`) and registers the endpoint itself. Total.js 5 apps keep routes in `controllers/`; use the `route:` property only in small apps that have no `controllers/` folder.

## Authentication

One `AUTH` in `definitions/auth.js`. It decides who the request is and calls `$.success(user)` or `$.invalid()`.

```js
AUTH(function($) {
	var token = $.headers['x-token'];
	if (token) {
		if (BLOCKED($, 10)) {      // too many wrong tries from this client
			$.invalid();
			return;
		}
		if (token === CONF.token) {
			BLOCKED($, -1);        // forget the failures
			$.success(BOT);
		} else
			$.invalid();
	} else
		$.invalid();
});
```

- The user object is small: `{ id, name, sa, permissions }`. `sa` marks a super administrator.
- Use `BLOCKED($, limit)` to rate-limit failed logins: it counts tries per `$.ip` and returns `true` once the limit is passed (`BLOCKED($, -1)` clears the count). Because it keys on `$.ip`, it inherits the `X-Forwarded-For` caveat below.
- `+` routes call `AUTH` first; actions then check `permissions`.
- `$.ip` takes the first value of `X-Forwarded-For`, which a client can forge. For security limits use `$.req.socket.remoteAddress`, or trust the header only behind your own proxy.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/conventions/main/backend/definitions-and-modules.md

# Definitions and modules

## definitions/

Files here are loaded when the app starts. They export nothing: they register things on the framework. One file per concern.

| File | Holds |
|---|---|
| `auth.js` | the single `AUTH(...)` |
| `init.js` | config defaults and `ON('ready', ...)`: load caches, register UI components |
| `func.js` | shared helpers as `FUNC.name = function() {}` |
| `db.js` | shared state objects (`MAIN.id`, `MAIN.db`) |

```js
// definitions/init.js
CONF.version = '1';
if (!CONF.cdn)
	CONF.cdn = 'https://cdn.componentator.com';

ON('ready', function() {
	setTimeout(FUNC.load, 500);
	COMPONENTATOR('ui', 'exec,locale,input,form,validate,...', true);
});
```

```js
// definitions/func.js
FUNC.refreshtags = async function() {
	REPO.tags = await DATA.find('tbl_tag').fields('id,search').promise();
};
```

- Helpers are named in lowercase without separators: `FUNC.refreshtags`, `FUNC.notify`.
- Use `ON('ready')` for anything that needs the app and the database to be up.
- `EMIT('configure')` / `ON('configure')` is how parts of the app react to a config change.

## config

A plain file, one `key : value` per line. Read it with `CONF.key`. Settings the framework owns start with `$`: `$api`, `$minifyjs`. Secrets (keys, database URLs) do not belong in a repository: keep them in the deployment config.

## modules/

A module is an integration with another system or a self-contained service (`cdn.js`, `openplatform.js`, `visitors.js`). It uses the same `exports.install` pattern as a controller and may add its own globals (`OpenPlatform`). Keep a module independent: it reads `CONF`, not other modules' internals.

## Shared state

- `MAIN`: the application's own state (`MAIN.db`, `MAIN.cache`).
- `REPO`: cached lookups that the UI also needs (`REPO.tags`, `REPO.ui`).
- `FUNC`: functions shared by actions and controllers.

Do not create new globals. Hang things from these three.

## Config in the database

When settings live in a table (`cl_config`), load them with `LOADCONFIG(rows)` and emit `configure`, as `FUNC.reconfigure` does in Todomator.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/conventions/main/backend/gotchas.md

# Gotchas of the server

Things that behave differently from what you would guess. Each one is a rule.

## Answers

- In an **action**, `$.callback(data)` returns data. In a plain **route handler** (`function($)`), `$.callback(err, value)` takes the error first: answer with `$.json(data)` instead.
- `$.invalid(404)`: a number above 399 sets the HTTP status (`$.invalid()` without an argument is 401). `$.invalid('@(text)')` answers with the message; its second argument is the `path` of the field the error belongs to, not a status code.
- On a handler you can also set the status yourself: `$.response.status = 401; $.json(...)`.

## Request data

- Route parameters (`{id}`) are in `$.params`.
- `$.body` is already parsed. The raw body (for webhook signatures) is `$.payload`, a Buffer.
- `$.ip` is the first `X-Forwarded-For` value: forgeable. Use `$.req.socket.remoteAddress` for security limits.
- The CSRF token is bound to the IP and `@{csrf}` can fail in views; pass `encodeURIComponent($.csrf())` through the repository.
- The session is bound to the user agent: a request with another user agent (a mobile emulation in a test browser) is unauthorized.

## Schemas and input

- A `Boolean` that is absent is `false`. Use `partial: true` when absence must mean "unchanged".
- With `partial`, a `null` number is ignored; use `0` for "none".
- `*field:[String]` rejects an empty list; drop the `*` if empty is allowed.
- Never `for...in` over an array. Use a classic `for` loop.

## Served JavaScript and static files

- The JavaScript minifier (on by default in release) can break code that `node --check` accepts: a regex literal containing `//` is cut as a comment (write `indexOf('https://')` instead), and spaces next to `${...}` in template literals are removed. Check the served file, or set `$minifyjs : false` in `config`.
- In release, static files are served from memory: restart the app after changing them. Browsers also cache: force a reload while testing.

## Data

- NoSQL: `NOSQL('x').find().where(...)`; `.sort(field, true)` is **descending**. Updates append a line and mark the old one, so the file grows until it is cleaned.
- NoSQL dates arrive on the server as `Date`, on the client as text.

## Tests

- `opt.config` passed to `Total.run` is overridden by `(env)` entries of the config: set `process.env` first.
- `total5 translate` scans the whole directory, `node_modules` included; run it on a copy of the sources or use a small script.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/conventions/main/database/sql-scripts.md

# SQL scripts (PostgreSQL)

Source: the [official guidelines](https://github.com/totaljs-es/guidelines) and the `database.sql` files of Todomator and OpenPlatform.

## Files

- `database.sql` holds the whole current schema, so a new installation needs one file.
- A change to an existing installation goes in a separate script next to it, named with a date: `database-2024-10-30.sql`. OpenPlatform does this; Todomator also has `database_1-5.sql` by version. Prefer the dated name with dashes, as the file rule requires.
- The first lines of an upgrade script say which version it upgrades from and that it must run before the app starts.
- Inside a script, order the objects: **tables, views, functions and stored procedures, indexes**, each part under a banner comment (`-- TABLES`, `-- VIEWS`, `-- INDEXES`).
- Todomator wraps its script in `BEGIN; ... COMMIT;` so that it applies completely or not at all.

## Names

All lowercase, singular.

| Object | Prefix | Example |
|---|---|---|
| table | `tbl_` | `tbl_user`, `tbl_ticket_time` |
| code list (rarely changes, used for choices) | `cl_` | `cl_status`, `cl_type` |
| view | `view_` | `view_ticket` |
| stored procedure | `sp_` | `sp_user` |
| function | `fn_` | `fn_user` |

Name indexes `<table>_idx<what>`: `tbl_ticket_idxstatus`. Name foreign keys `<table>_<column>_fkey`.

## Columns

- Type `text`, not `varchar`. Lists are `_text`, structured data `json` or `jsonb`, small numbers `int2`, dates `timestamp`, flags `bool`.
- `id` is the primary key, `text`, filled in the code with `UID()`. A foreign key is the table plus `id`: `userid`, `folderid`, `parentid`.
- Dates start with `dt`: `dtcreated`, `dtupdated`, `dtremoved`. Booleans start with `is`: `isremoved`, `ispublic`, `isdisabled`.
- Use the same names for the same thing in every table: `name`, `body`, `search`, `sortindex`, `icon`, `color`.
- When it fits, every table has `id`, `name` and `dtcreated`.
- `dtcreated` defaults to UTC now: `DEFAULT timezone('utc'::text, now())`.
- A column that lists search keywords is called `search`.

## Order of the columns

Identifiers first, then main fields, numbers, booleans, and dates last. Then the constraints and the primary key.

```sql
CREATE TABLE "public"."tbl_ticket" (
	"id" text NOT NULL,
	"folderid" text,
	"ownerid" text,
	"name" text,
	"search" text,
	"attrs" json,
	"worked" int4 DEFAULT 0,
	"ispublic" bool DEFAULT false,
	"isremoved" bool DEFAULT false,
	"dtupdated" timestamp,
	"dtcreated" timestamp DEFAULT timezone('utc'::text, now()),
	CONSTRAINT "tbl_ticket_folderid_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("folderid") REFERENCES "public"."tbl_folder"("id") ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
	PRIMARY KEY ("id")
);
```

## Code lists

A `cl_` table holds the choices of the app and is read once into memory.

```sql
CREATE TABLE "public"."cl_status" (
	"id" text NOT NULL,
	"name" text,
	"icon" text,
	"color" text,
	"sortindex" int2 DEFAULT 0,
	PRIMARY KEY ("id")
);
```

## Format

Tabs (width 4), no useless casts (`name <> 'x'`, not `name <> 'x'::text`), one statement per `;`, a trailing `;` on every command.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/conventions/main/database/queries.md

# Queries with `DATA`

Total.js talks to PostgreSQL through `DATA`, a query builder. Use it for everything it can express; write raw SQL only for what it cannot.

Always end with `.promise($)` (in an async action) or `.callback($)`. Passing `$` lets the framework answer the request with the error.

## Read

```js
// one record
var item = await DATA.read('tbl_user').fields('id,name').id(params.id).error('@(User not found)').promise($);

// several
var items = await DATA.find('tbl_tag').fields('id,search').where('folderid', id).promise($);

// values from a list
var apps = await DATA.find('op.tbl_app_permission').fields('id,appid').in('id', permissions).promise($);
```

- `.fields('a,b')` selects columns; name them, do not read `*`.
- `.id(value)` filters by the primary key.
- `.error('@(text)')` or `.error(404)` answers with that error when nothing is found. It is what turns a missing row into a 404.

## A list for the UI

`autoquery` reads the query string (`?q=`, `sort`, `page`, `limit`) and builds the query. Name the allowed fields and their types, a default sort and a maximum page size:

```js
NEWACTION('Groups|list', {
	name: 'List of groups',
	action: function($) {
		DATA.find('op.view_group').autoquery($.query, 'id:UID,name,color,icon,users:Number,dtcreated:Date,dtupdated:Date', 'dtcreated_desc', 100).callback($);
	}
});
```

A list that joins several tables reads from a `view_`.

## Write

```js
model.id = UID();
model.dtcreated = NOW;
await DATA.insert('tbl_ticket_time', model).promise($);

model.dtupdated = NOW;
await DATA.modify('op.tbl_group', model).id(params.id).error('@(Group not found)').promise($);

await DATA.remove('tbl_tag').id(params.id).error(404).promise($);
await DATA.remove('tbl_notification').where('ticketid', params.id).where('typeid', 'logwork').promise($);
```

- Fill `id` with `UID()` and the dates with `NOW` in the action, not in the database.
- Remove fields that are not columns before `insert` / `modify` (`model.permissions = undefined`).
- Update or insert in one call: `DATA.modify('tbl_x', data, true).id(id).insert(fn, params)`.

## Conditions

`where(field, value)`, `in(field, array)`, `notin(field, array)`, `search(field, keyword)`, `or(function(b) { b.search('name', m); b.search('email', m); })`.

```js
var keywords = text.toKeywords(true, true);
for (var i = 0; i < keywords.length; i++)
	builder.search('a.search', keywords[i]);
```

## Raw SQL

`DATA.query('UPDATE tbl_ticket a SET worked=(SELECT ...) WHERE a.id=$1', [id]).promise($)`.

- Prefer parameters (`$1`) over building the text.
- When a value must go into the text, escape it with `PG_ESCAPE(value)` before `.format()`. Never concatenate user input.

## Schemas (namespaces)

A table can be addressed with its schema: `op.tbl_user`. Keep the prefix consistent inside one file.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/conventions/main/frontend/components.md

# Components (jComponent)

For widgets, forms, lists, inputs and every other piece of UI, **use a component that already exists**. If none fits, **create a component** (do not build the piece with ad hoc markup and scripts). Load components with `COMPONENTATOR()`, always.

## 1. Look for the component first

The catalogue of jComponent components, with the options and examples of each, is in Forge: <https://forge.totaljs.es/es/components/> (also in `/en/components/`).

Before writing UI:

1. Find the component that does the job (input, form, listing, datagrid, notify, menu, approve...).
2. Read its page: what it does, its **configuration** and its context (what path and data it expects, what it needs around it).
3. Use it from markup with `<ui-component name="..." path="..." config="...">`.

Machine-readable forms of the same catalogue (use these from code or an agent):

| What | URL |
|---|---|
| One component as markdown | `https://forge.totaljs.es/en/components/<name>.md` (e.g. `input.md`) |
| The whole catalogue as one text | `https://forge.totaljs.es/llms-components.txt` |
| The catalogue as JSON lines | `https://forge.totaljs.es/components/dataset.jsonl` |
| Index of all Forge pages | `https://forge.totaljs.es/index.json` |

Each page carries its framework version (`jcomponent@20`) and a content hash, so you can tell which version a rule refers to.

## Preferred components

When several components could do the job, use these:

| For | Use | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Form fields (text, email, phone, password, multiline, checkbox, select, date...) | `input` (j-Input) | One component for every field: `type` chooses the kind. It replaces j-Textbox and j-Dropdown. |
| A box with a fixed height and scroll | `viewbox` | `height` is a percentage, `parent` is the container (or `window`), `scroll` / `scrollbar` control scrolling. |
| Loaders | `loading` | Reacts to the `@showloading` and `@hideloading` flags; `style` picks the look (1 = spinner, 2 = line at the top). |
| Tables and data grids | `datagrid` | For single page and enterprise apps: filters, sorting, pages, `height` modes (`auto`, `fluid`, `parent`). |
| Buttons and calls to functions | `exec` | See below. |
| Predefined design (panels, toolbars, badges, messages, listings, tabs, dark mode) | `intranetcss` | Ready-made CSS classes; see below. |

### exec: buttons and function calls

`exec` is a singleton that works for the whole page: any element with the class `exec` calls a function when it is clicked. Do not add `onclick` handlers or `addEventListener` for buttons.

```html
<button class="exec" data-exec="?/create"><i class="ti ti-plus-circle"></i>@(Create)</button>
<span class="exec" data-exec="?/options" data-prevent="true">...</span>
<a class="exec" data-href="/offers/">@(Offers)</a>
```

- `data-exec="NAME"`: the function to call, with the form `function(element, event)`. A `?` calls a method of the current plugin (`?/create` is `exports.create`).
- `data-prevent="true"`: stops the click from going further (for a button inside a clickable row).
- `data-href="URL"`: redirects instead of calling a function.
- Double click and context menu use the same attributes with a suffix: `data-exec2` (class `exec2`) and `data-exec3` (class `exec3`).

### intranetcss: predefined design

`intranetcss` is a component made only of CSS. It brings the shared look of the intranet apps, with a dark mode, so a screen does not need its own style for the common pieces:

- containers: `.panel` (with `label` and `.toolbar`), `.padding`, `.divider`, `.bg-smoke`
- lists and menus: `.listing`, `.listing2`, `.nav`, `.tabmenu`, `.tabmenu2`, `.iconmenu`, `.keyvalue`
- messages and badges: `.message`, `.message-success`, `.message-error`, `.message-alert`, `.badge` (with colors and sizes)
- sizes: `.small`, `.medium`, `.large`

Use these classes before writing new CSS (see [css](css.md)). The component is not in the Forge catalogue; its source (version 5) is served by the component download service.

## 2. If it does not exist, create a component

A piece of UI that has behaviour is a component, not a block of script inside a page.

```js
COMPONENT('name', function(self, config, cls) {
	// keep the names: "self", "config" and "cls"
});
```

- Names of components, plugins, variables and settings in **lowercase**.
- Keep at most 2-3 levels of nesting in objects.
- Avoid `_` in variable names.
- **Think reusable**: a component takes its data from `path` and its options from `config`, and knows nothing about the screen that uses it.
- Use the same name across projects for the same thing. Check the catalogue before choosing one.

## 3. Load components with COMPONENTATOR()

Never link a component file by hand. List the components the app uses in `definitions/init.js`:

```js
ON('ready', function() {
	COMPONENTATOR('ui', 'exec,locale,page,viewbox,input,form,validate,loading,datagrid,intranetcss,message,menu,approve,notify,errorhandler', true);
});
```

`COMPONENTATOR(name, components, removeprev, attrs)`:

- `name`: the name of the bundle (`'ui'`).
- `components`: the components of the bundle, comma-separated, without the `j-` prefix.
- `removeprev` (default `true`): deletes the older bundles of the same name when the list changes.
- `attrs`: optional extra parameters for the bundle.

The framework downloads the bundle once, saves it in `public/` as `ui-<name>-<hash>.min.js` and stores its address in `REPO.<name>`. The layout loads it:

```html
<script src="@{REPO.ui}"></script>
```

Rules:

- One `COMPONENTATOR()` call per bundle (`ui` for the app, `webui` for public pages).
- List **only** the components the app uses: the bundle is what every user downloads.
- When you start using a component, add it to the list; when no screen uses it any more, remove it.
- A component you created yourself is a normal file of the app (`public/` or the plugin's `public/`), not a `COMPONENTATOR()` entry.

## 4. Quick check

- Is there a component for this in the catalogue? Use it.
- Did you read its configuration and context before using it? Do.
- Is it in the `COMPONENTATOR()` list? Add it.
- Is there none? Create a reusable `COMPONENT('name', ...)` and use it from markup.

See [plugins-ui](plugins-ui.md) for how screens and forms use components, and [views-and-layout](views-and-layout.md) for the layout that loads the bundle.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/conventions/main/frontend/plugins-ui.md

# Plugins with UI

A feature of an app is a **plugin**: a folder with a server part and a UI part that the framework loads and the app shell mounts. The CMS admin (pages, layouts, redirects, settings...) and the Todomator users screen are made this way.

```
plugins/redirects/
	index.js              server: metadata + routes
	schemas/redirects.js  actions (see backend/actions.md)
	public/index.html     the screen: markup + <script>PLUGIN(...)</script>
	public/form.html      the form that opens over the screen
```

## Server part: index.js

```js
exports.icon = 'ti ti-exchange';
exports.name = '@(Redirects)';
exports.position = 3;
exports.permissions = [{ id: 'redirects', name: 'Redirects' }];
exports.visible = function(user) {
	return user.sa || user.permissions.indexOf('redirects') !== -1 || user.permissions.indexOf('admin') !== -1;
};

exports.install = function() {
	ROUTE('+API    ?    -redirects_list               --> Redirects|list');
	ROUTE('+API    ?    +redirects_save               --> Redirects|save');
};
```

- `icon` is a Tabler icon class (`ti ti-name`), `name` is translatable with `@(...)`, `position` orders the menu.
- `permissions` declares what the plugin adds; `visible` decides who sees it.
- Routes use the same syntax as everywhere (see [routes-and-auth](../backend/routes-and-auth.md)).

## UI part: a screen

A screen is HTML with a `<ui-plugin>` root and one `PLUGIN(function(exports) { ... })` block. Keep markup, scoped style and logic in the same file.

```html
<style>
	.CLASS .listing2 figure { margin-bottom: 10px; }
</style>

<ui-plugin class="CLASS bg-white">
	<ui-component name="empty" path="?.items" config="parent:auto" class="invisible">
		...
	</ui-component>
</ui-plugin>

<script>
	PLUGIN(function(exports) {

		exports.reload = function() {
			exports.refresh();
		};

		exports.refresh = function() {
			exports.tapi('redirects_list', function(response) {
				exports.set('items', response);
			});
		};

	});
</script>
```

Rules:

- `CLASS` in selectors and class lists is replaced with a unique class for the plugin: it scopes the CSS so plugins do not collide.
- `?` in a path (`?.items`, `?/create`) means "this plugin": `?.items` is the data, `?/create` is `exports.create`.
- `exports.reload` runs every time the screen opens.
- Call the server with `exports.tapi('endpoint_name', data, callback)`. Add `ERROR` after the name (`'redirects_read ERROR'`) to show an error message to the user automatically.
- Set data with `exports.set('items', value)`, or globally with `SET('path @reset', value)`; read the model with `exports.model`.
- Handlers are attached in markup: `class="exec" data-exec="?/edit" data-id="{{ m.id }}"`. Read the attribute with `ATTRD(el)`.
- Text for people is always `@(Text)` so it can be translated.
- Naming: plugin, component and global names in **lowercase**; keep the names `exports`, `self`, `config`, `cls` as they are.

Official guide on names:

```js
// BAD
PLUGIN('Name', function(plugin) { plugin.doSomething = function() {}; });

// GOOD
PLUGIN('name', function(exports) { exports.dosomething = function() {}; });
```

## A form

A form is a second file loaded with an `importer` and shown by `miniform` / `form`. It has `?.field` inputs, a `validate` that enables the submit button, and a `submit` function.

```html
<ui-component name="miniform" path="common.form" config="if:CLASS;icon:ti ti-exchange;autofocus:true;reload:?/reload;submit:?/submit;width:400" class="hidden" plugin="CLASS">
	<div class="padding">
		<div class="m">
			<ui-component name="input" path="?.url" config="required:1;placeholder:@(Relative URL address)">@(URL)</ui-component>
		</div>
	</div>
	<nav>
		<ui-component name="validate" path="?">
			<button name="submit" disabled><i class="ti ti-check-circle"></i>@(SUBMIT)</button>
			<button name="cancel">@(Cancel)</button>
		</ui-component>
	</nav>
</ui-component>
```

Open it from the screen:

```js
exports.create = function() {
	SET('formredirect @default', {});
	SET('*form', 'formredirect');
};
```

## Confirm and menu

```js
SETTER('approve/show', '@(Are you sure you want to remove it?)', ':ti ti-trash: @(Remove)', function() {
	exports.tapi('redirects_remove/ ERROR', { id: id }, function() { exports.refresh(); });
});
SETTER('menu/show', opt);
```

## Think reusable

Components, plugins and global names are shared across projects. Before inventing one, look in the [catalogue of components](components.md) and in another app for the same name.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/conventions/main/frontend/views-and-layout.md

# Views and layout

## Layout

The shell of an app is one HTML file in `views/` (`admin.html`, `index.html`). It sets the title, loads the UI library, registers global components once and mounts the plugins.

```html
@{layout('')}
@{title(config.name)}

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
	<meta charset="utf-8" />
	<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
	<link href="@{'%cdn'}/spa.min@19.css" rel="stylesheet" />
	<script src="@{'%cdn'}/spa.min@19.js"></script>
	<script src="@{REPO.ui}"></script>
	@{import('meta', 'head', 'default.js + func.js', 'default.css', 'favicon.ico')}
</head>
<body class="invisible">

	<ui-component name="exec"></ui-component>
	<ui-component name="errorhandler"></ui-component>
	<ui-component name="locale" config="requests:1;language:@{language}"></ui-component>
	<ui-component name="LAZY menu" config="style:2"></ui-component>

</body>
</html>
```

- Directives start with `@{...}`: `@{title()}`, `@{import()}`, `@{if}` / `@{fi}`, `@{REPO.ui}`, `@{'%cdn'}` (a config value).
- Global components are declared once in the layout. `LAZY` loads a component only when it is first used.
- The component bundle is loaded with `COMPONENTATOR('ui', 'exec,locale,input,...', true)` in `definitions/init.js`. List only the components the app uses; see [components](components.md).
- `<body class="invisible">` hides the page until the UI is ready.

## Translations

Every text a person reads is wrapped in `@(...)`, in views, in plugin HTML and in server messages: `@(Save)`. The text in English is the key.

## Two kinds of pages

- **App screens** (admin, tools): plugin HTML mounted in the layout, driven by `PLUGIN`.
- **Public pages**: server-rendered views returned by a controller (`$.view('index')`) or compiled from the CMS. They carry no `PLUGIN` logic.

## Naming

Lowercase file names with `-`: `search-results.html`, `form-offer.html`.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/conventions/main/frontend/css.md

# CSS

Source: the [official guidelines](https://github.com/totaljs-es/guidelines).

- File names lowercase, words separated by `-`.
- **One rule per line**: keep all declarations of a selector on the same line.
- Strings in `'` apostrophes.
- No vendor prefixes. Put `/*auto*/` at the top of the file and Total.js adds them.
- No LESS and no SASS: Total.js CSS supports variables and nested selectors.

```css
/*auto*/

.class { key1: value; key2: value; key3: value; }
.class > div { key1: value; key2: value; }
```

## In plugins

Style that belongs to a screen goes at the top of its HTML file, scoped with `CLASS`:

```html
<style>
	.CLASS .listing2 figure { margin-bottom: 10px; }
	.CLASS .listing2 .permanent { background-color: #F6E7EA; }
</style>
```

`CLASS` becomes a class unique to the plugin, so the rule cannot leak to other screens.

## Predefined classes

The `intranetcss` component provides the common design (panels, toolbars, badges, messages, listings, tabs, dark mode). Use its classes before writing new CSS: see [components](components.md).

## Global style

`public/default.css` holds what is shared. Colors that change per user or theme are CSS variables (`:root { --color: ... }`), set once in the layout.

## Static files

`/img/`, `/css/`, `/js/`, `/fonts/`, `/videos/`. Images use the file-name rule: lowercase with dashes.
